title: Progress Test 6
canDo: I can handle shopping, services and everyday objects in English.
objectives: I can handle shopping, services and everyday objects in English.
complete the three assessment parts with clear evidence
use the target grammar and vocabulary from the scope
materials: A2 speaking rubric, task cards, timer, progress record.
assessment: A2 speaking rubric: 4 criteria, 1-4 points, 16 total. Pass: 10-12, no criterion below 2.

differentiation.individual: Use the teacher as the partner and allow longer turns. Keep the same rubric.
differentiation.group: Use pairs and rotate roles so every learner completes both sides.
differentiation.children: Not applicable: this assessment is designed for adults.
differentiation.teens: Use the same tasks with age-appropriate topics and a shorter Part C.
differentiation.adults: Use the tasks as written; keep the scenarios realistic and respectful.
differentiation.seniors: Allow extra preparation time and large-print task cards.

links.phonetics: Clear sentence stress and polite intonation in the assessment tasks.

elements.content: Assessment: Progress Test 6

Scope: Units 11-12: shopping, services and things
Time: 45 minutes
Format: pair work with assessor observation
Rubric: 4 criteria, 1-4 points, 16 total. A2 pass: 10-12 points, no criterion below 2.
By the end of this assessment, you can:

• I can handle shopping, services and everyday objects in English.
• complete the three assessment parts with clear evidence
• use the target grammar and vocabulary from the scope

teacher_notes.title: Assessment setup
teacher_notes.content: Set up pairs and explain the three parts. Keep the rubric visible. Do not correct during the tasks.

teacher_notes.title: Rubric discussion
teacher_notes.content: Ask: 'Which criterion do you want to show today? Why?' Take two answers and note them for feedback.

teacher_notes.title: Timing discussion
teacher_notes.content: Ask: 'How will you use your preparation time?' Remind students that 45 minutes includes all three parts.

teacher_notes.title: Monolingual rule
teacher_notes.content: If a student uses L1, prompt in English: 'How can you say that another way?' Score monolingual independence under criterion 4.

elements.content: Score each criterion from 1 to 4. A2 pass: 10-12 total, no criterion below 2.

Task completion: 4 = all parts + natural follow-ups; 3 = main task + one follow-up; 2 = short answers, partner leads; 1 = one-word or memorised answers.
Grammar control: 4 = present, past and future accurate most of the time; 3 = present and basic past controlled; 2 = mostly Present Simple, frequent verb errors; 1 = isolated words.
Vocabulary & chunks: 4 = topic collocations + clear paraphrasing; 3 = enough everyday vocabulary + taught frames; 2 = basic words, long searches; 1 = survival words only.
Fluency & monolingual independence: 4 = connected phrases, natural pauses, zero L1; 3 = planning pauses but steady, stays in English; 2 = frequent restarts, some listener effort; 1 = fragmented speech, relies on L1 or gestures.
Evidence to listen for:

• Follow-up questions and reactions
• Target grammar in extended turns
• Topic collocations and paraphrasing
• English-only strategies when stuck

teacher_notes.title: Rubric walkthrough
teacher_notes.content: Read each criterion aloud and give one example of a 4 and a 2. Check that students understand 'paraphrase' and 'follow-up question'.

teacher_notes.title: Score discussion
teacher_notes.content: Ask: 'What does a solid A2 answer sound like?' Elicit that it is not perfect; it is clear, connected and keeps going.

teacher_notes.title: Evidence discussion
teacher_notes.content: Ask: 'Which evidence will you show in Part B?' Link answers to the role-play and decision tasks.

slides.title: 3. Part A: Shopping and services interview

elements.content: Part A: Shopping and services interview (about 3 minutes)
Tell your partner about a recent purchase or service problem. What happened, and how was it solved? Partner, ask two follow-up questions.
Follow-up prompts:

• Have you ... yet?
• Could you ...?
• What would you do next time?

teacher_notes.title: Part A setup
teacher_notes.content: Give students one minute to think, then start. The partner must ask at least two follow-up questions.

teacher_notes.title: Discussion
teacher_notes.content: Ask: 'Which follow-up question worked best? Why?' Use the answers to model natural interaction.

teacher_notes.title: Evidence discussion
teacher_notes.content: Ask: 'Which criterion did Part A show most clearly?' Note one example per student for the rubric.

elements.content: Part B: Service desk role-play (about 4-5 minutes)

Student A: You bought headphones yesterday and one side does not work. You have the receipt. Ask politely for an exchange or refund.

Student B: You are the service assistant. Ask for the receipt, explain the policy, and offer one solution. Use polite requests.
Task check:

• Complete both roles
• Ask at least one follow-up question
• Use the target grammar and vocabulary
• Reach a clear agreement or outcome

teacher_notes.title: Role-play setup
teacher_notes.content: Assign A and B. Give one minute of preparation. Monitor without joining unless the pair is stuck.

teacher_notes.title: Discussion
teacher_notes.content: Ask: 'Which part was harder: explaining or asking questions?' Discuss why both matter in real conversation.

teacher_notes.title: Monitoring discussion
teacher_notes.content: Ask: 'What language helped you reach an agreement?' Collect two useful phrases for the board.

elements.content: Part C: Describe and guess (about 2-3 minutes)
Describe two everyday objects, apps or services without naming them. Use who, which, that or where. Your partner guesses.
Useful language:

• It's a thing that ...
• It's a place where ...
• It's someone who ...

teacher_notes.title: Part C setup
teacher_notes.content: Keep this part short and timed. The aim is fluency and clear communication, not perfection.

teacher_notes.title: Discussion
teacher_notes.content: Ask: 'Which phrase helped you keep going when you did not know a word?' Share two strategies.

teacher_notes.title: Timing discussion
teacher_notes.content: Ask: 'Did you finish in time? What would you cut or add?' Use the answers for the next assessment.

elements.content: Score each criterion after the task, not during it.

Criterion 1: task completion and interaction
Criterion 2: grammar control
Criterion 3: vocabulary and functional chunks
Criterion 4: fluency, pronunciation and monolingual independence
Evidence notes:
Write one example for each criterion. Include one strength and one next step. Do not write a full transcript.

teacher_notes.title: Scoring guidance
teacher_notes.content: Score the whole performance, not one mistake. A student who communicates clearly with minor errors can still score 3.

teacher_notes.title: Moderation discussion
teacher_notes.content: Ask: 'Where is the line between 2 and 3 for grammar?' Discuss one example and agree on a consistent standard.

teacher_notes.title: Evidence discussion
teacher_notes.content: Ask: 'Which evidence is strongest: the role-play or the story?' Explain that different tasks show different criteria.

elements.content: Give two concrete takeaways: one strength and one next step.
Example: Strength: you switched from Present Perfect to Past Simple smoothly. Next step: use going to for future plans.
Student self-assessment:

I can keep the conversation going.
I can use the target grammar without stopping.
I can explain a word in English when I do not know it.
I can ask at least one follow-up question.

teacher_notes.title: Feedback discussion
teacher_notes.content: Ask: 'Which strength are you most proud of? Which next step will you practise first?' Keep the feedback specific and positive.

teacher_notes.title: Goal discussion
teacher_notes.content: Ask: 'What will you do this week to improve your next step?' Ask each student to name one concrete action.

teacher_notes.title: Record keeping
teacher_notes.content: Record the four scores, the total, and the two takeaways in the learner's progress record.

elements.content: Homework:
Write a 70-90 word polite message to a service desk about a problem. Include two requests with could / would it be possible.
Recycling into the next lesson:
Next lesson recycles shopping vocabulary, quantifiers and relative clauses.

teacher_notes.title: Homework discussion
teacher_notes.content: Ask: 'When and where will you do the homework? What might stop you?' Ask each student to name one concrete plan.

teacher_notes.title: Recycling discussion
teacher_notes.content: Ask: 'Which language from today will you use in the next lesson?' Link the answer to the next unit.

teacher_notes.title: Reassessment
teacher_notes.content: If a student scores below 10, plan a short reassessment after two weeks of focused practice.
